author: Billy Dukes
title: Shots Fired! Morgan Wallen Makes Feelings About Charley Crockett Clear - NewsBreak
text:
By Billy Dukes ,
7 hours ago Getty Images Morgan Wallen fans in Toronto didn’t get to hear the singer’s response to Charley Crockett . They got to see it.
If anything was spoken about the controversy around Crockett and Gavin Adcock (and tangentially, Wallen) during a Sept. 4 concert, it hasn’t appeared on social media. Instead, there’s video of Wallen giving two middle fingers to a Charley Crockett T-shirt.
In June, Gavin Adcock criticized Beyoncé’s Cowboy Carter album, which — at the time — was one spot above his yet-to-be-released Own Worst Enemy album on Apple Music’s Country Albums chart. Last month, Crockett took to Instagram to point out the hypocrisy of the wider argument that Beyoncé and her album should not be labeled “country.” He never mentioned Adcock but did seem to point to him. Wallen was brought into the conversation when Crockett says, “#1 country artist on earth listens to nothing but rap. Openly says he doesn’t really know any country music. Gotta respect his honesty.” Related : Who Is Charley Crockett?
In the video, tour opener Adcock approaches Wallen with a Crockett T-shirt and the “I’m the Problem” singer gives it two middle fingers and skips away in the other direction.
@maryanna_khnanisho I wanna know the story behind the shirt tho #morganwallen #fyp #toronto @morganwallen @GavinAdcockMusic
♬ original sound – maryanna
Since an August Instagram post, Crockett hasn’t spoken directly about a controversy created by him and Adcock.
The country newcomer (who’s managed by Wallen’s management team) has carried on with several posts criticizing Crockett, labeling him a “cosplay cowboy” and claiming he was left flowers and an album as an olive branch.
Last Thursday’s moment in Toronto was the first time Wallen addressed it all.
Worth noting is that both Adcock and Crockett released new albums in August. It’s not clear how popular Adcock’s feelings are toward the Texan among his own fans. Posts on social media have been roundly criticized in the past.
10 Gavin Adcock Songs Every New Fan Should Hear A traditionalist at heart who's also not afraid to push genre boundaries and incorporate novel sounds, Gavin Adcock is walking his own line in country music.
What other country artists incorporate grunge rock, blues and yodeling — sometimes even in the same song? Keep reading for a primer on the 10 best Gavin Adcock songs to listen to if you want to get a taste of what this buzzy newcomer is all about. Gallery Credit: Carena Liptak Bert Kreischer, YouTube "Deep End" Adock's got 99 problems in this 2023 fan-favorite — and demons, drugs and bad choices are at least three of them. Add in some rock guitars and impressive high notes, and he's got a hit. Meateater Podcast, YouTube "Don't Run Your Mouth" Adcock could easily fall into that category of radio hitmakers that also includes rock-curious new outlaws like Jackson Dean and Warren Zeiders. But songs like "Don't Run Your Mouth" prove this Georgia boy has a personality all his own. A bluesy melody and a little yodel on the vocals make this song stand out. Jeff Schear, Getty Images "Ain't No Cure" This is one of Adcock's most-streamed songs, and it's easy to see why: "Ain't No Cure" is pure, acoustic country-rock magic. Danielle Del Valle, Getty Images "Four Leaf Clover" "Four Leaf Clover" comes off Adcock's 2024 Actin' Up Again , and like all his best songs, it's got a twist. The title implies good luck, but in this story, "luck" might not be the thing he needs to save his tumultuous relationship. Grand Ole Opry, YouTube "A Cigarette" Racking up more than 30 million streams in just a few months, this lovelorn ballad is the song that proved that Adcock is truly on his way to establishing his superstardom. CTFestivals, YouTube "On One" Grunge rock isn't a genre tangent most country stars go down, but it's a great template for this new song from Adcock, providing the perfect musical backdrop for his just-don't-give-a-damn lyrics. Tracy Lawrence, YouTube "Never Call Again" Gavin Adcock's discography is full of tough rock songs about demons and bravado, but he never forgets to let a little tenderness show, either. Adcock isn't afraid to admit his heartbreak in "Never Call Again." Danielle Del Valle, Getty Images "Unlucky Strikes" This bad-timing song is actually pretty fun to sing along to! It's also a dose of classic tear-in-your-beer country, with a dancehall twist. Jeff Schear, Getty Images "Need To" In this early-2025 release, Adcock sings about drinking his troubles away at the recommendation of an unlikely source: His mama!
Fun fact: Songwriting great Casey Beathard and his singer-songwriter son Tucker Beathard were two of the writers on this track. Danielle Del Valle, Getty Images "Sober" " Might end up in jail, hell, I might even cry ," Adcock sings in "Sober": A song that delivers an exquisite blend of grizzled masculinity and tender, reflective emotion. The Top 10 Charley Crockett Songs Every New Fan Should Hear To a sub-sect of alt-country fans, Crockett is one of the biggest names in the business. The Texas-born crooner is one of the genre's most authentic cowboy stars, and he's won multiple awards in the Americana format. But to mainstream listeners and terrestrial radio, Crockett's music is still uncharted territory. Keep scrolling for a primer on the best Charley Crockett songs for a new fan. Gallery Credit: Carena Liptak Rich Fury, Getty Images "Welcome to Hard Times" The title track of Crockett's 2020 Welcome to Hard Times album is equal parts dark and fun. For a honky-tonkin' good time with a dash of sin, topped off with tinkling piano, look no further. Terry Wyatt, Getty Images "In the Night" An early-career song, "In the Night" shows off Crockett's bluesy side. Tom Cooper, Getty Images "The Man From Waco" This song is heavy on the "Western" half of "Country & Western." They just don't make 'em like this anymore. Erika Goldring, Getty Images "The Poplar Tree" A story song that would feel at home on a 1950s country record, "The Poplar Tree" is perfectly brooding and sad. Terry Wyatt, Getty Images "Trinity River" You can hear Charley Crockett's love of New Orleans and Creole music in this fun track. Jason Kempin, Getty Images "Borrowed Time" Honky-tonk your worries away with this fiddle-heavy tune about a love that's real, even though it's doomed. Emma McIntyre, Getty Images "Music City USA" " I shouldn't have come here in the first place / 'Cause folks in here don't like my kind ," Crockett sings in this caustic take-down of the music industry in Nashville. Crockett once backed out of a Sony record deal because he didn't want to play the corporate music game, so he comes by the sentiment in this song honestly. Rich Fury, Getty Images "I Am Not Afraid" There aren't too many out-and-out sweet love songs in Charley Crockett's discography, but this is one of them. Jason Kempin, Getty Images "I'm Just a Clown" Crockett plays the role of a comedic clown in this song -- but like every circus show, there's a little sadness hanging behind the bright colors and jokes. Rich Fury, Getty Images "Jamestown Ferry" Charley Crockett came up in music as a busker and traveling performer, so it only seems right to include one of his covers in this list. We're partial to Crockett's take on Tanya Tucker's "The Jamestown Ferry."
